Camera FOV Lab

How the companion turns a marker's pixel position into metres, why that depends on one number in companion.conf, and exactly where it goes wrong when that number is off. Every panel is live: drag the sliders or press play for the narrated tour in Russian.

Pinhole model: where the error is born

f = 640 / tan(FOV/2)

Top: the same pixel offset placed on an image plane at the real f and at the program's f. Bottom: angle error across the frame height. It is zero at the centre and grows toward the edges.

The calculation, step by step

tracker.cpp → mission.cpp

“Correct FOV” is the code fed with the real camera's angle. “Config FOV” is the same code fed with camera_hfov_deg. The first row where they differ is where the error enters.

Flight above the marker

simplified simulation of Mission::update
t = 0.0 s

Grey drone: config equals the real camera. Magenta drone: the config FOV from the slider. Both start 1.2 m behind and 2 m left of the marker at 7 m, gimbal at −75°, and run the real mission rules: HOVER inside 0.35 m, back to APPROACH beyond 0.7 m, descend after 3 s, hand over to PX4 at 1.5 m above the marker.

What to remember

  • The error is born on one line of src/tracker.cpp, where f is computed from camera_hfov_deg. Everything after it is correct maths on a wrong number.
  • The image never changes. A wrong FOV changes the ruler the program measures the image with, not the image.
  • Zero at the centre, worse toward the edges, with opposite signs above and below. The tilt gimbal hides it forward by centring the marker vertically; nothing hides it sideways.
  • Use the horizontal FOV of the frame the program receives. Not the diagonal, and not the sensor's full FOV if the video mode crops.
  • To check it, place the marker at a measured distance off to the side of the frame centre and compare the TARGET readout in the GUI window.

The flight panel is a simplified model: PX4 tracks velocity with a 0.4 s lag, video runs at 30 fps with the latency you set, the gimbal is ideal, and there is no wind or lens distortion. It shows the direction and rough size of the effect, not a flight-test result.
